subject: Re: Brightpath Dedicated fleet — proposal to rebalance SKU mix and sizing
messages:
From: Brightpath AI Ops <ops@brightpath.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurements@brightpath.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated fleet usage drop — options to rebalance

Hi Olga / Karthik,

We ran an internal review of October usage and saw a consistent downward shift in daytime utilization for our inference endpoints (p50 latency steady, but token volume down ~36% month-over-month). We currently run a 60 H100 reserve + 20 H100 burst layout under our Dedicated contract (BRP-8421). Given the lower sustained concurrency, finance is asking whether we can shift capacity to a mixed-sku approach to reduce unit costs while preserving tail latency for peak inference windows.

Quick asks:
- Can Redwood run a sizing analysis that maps our recent 90-day utilization profile to a proposed mix (A100/A10x/H100) and expected p95 latency?
- What would be the expected per-token $ delta for the typical 60/20 footprint vs a 40 H100 + 80 A100 mix?
- Can we pilot a gradual SKU shift (non-disruptive) and keep a temporary hot-standby in H100 for 30 days?

Attached: brightpath_current_utilization.csv (90-day aggregation).

Thanks — happy to set a 30-min sync if useful.

— Priya on behalf of Brightpath Ops
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Brightpath AI Ops <ops@brightpath.ai>, procurements@brightpath.ai
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated fleet usage drop — options to rebalance

Hi Priya (and team),

Thanks for the utilization CSV — useful signal. We built a small first-pass model (attached) that translates the 90-day profile into steady-state slots, expected batching efficiency, and p95 latency projections across three candidate mixes. High level takeaways:

- A partial shift from H100 to A100 for baseline steady-state should reduce per-token cost by ~18–22% depending on batching; impact on p95 is minimal when a hot-standby of H100 is retained for tail requests.
- For your observed daytime drop, we recommend a hybrid: reduce reserved H100 from 60 -> 40, increase A100 capacity (baseline) to absorb steady requests, keep a 20-H100 hot-standby buffer for peaks for 30 days.
- We can implement this as a staged rollout:
  1) Pilot: reassign 10 reserved H100 to A100-equivalent slots (observability enabled). 7 days monitoring.
  2) If stable, shift the remaining 10 H100 of reserved capacity over 14 days.
  3) Maintain 20 H100 hot-standby (billing-pro-rated) for 30 days before full conversion.

I've attached: redwood_capacity_model_v1.xlsx with the scenario breakdown and expected costs.

Next steps I propose:
1) Karthik / David to approve the M.A.P. (mutual action plan) and sign the amendment for the pilot.
2) Brightpath to confirm acceptable thresholds for p95 and an internal success metric (e.g., <10% increase in p95, or <5% of requests hitting hot-standby).
3) Schedule a 30-min kickoff the week of Oct 26 to align telemetry and billing proration approach.

Happy to walk through the spreadsheets on the call — I think there's a low-risk path to save you material cost while preserving SLA windows.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 29 Oct 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated fleet usage drop — options to rebalance

Folks — looping in a concrete proposal and the commercial framing so procurement can move quickly. See summary below and attached PDF.

Proposal summary (BRP-8421 amendment):
- Pilot tranche: convert 10 reserved H100 -> A100-equivalent reserved capacity (no SLA change) for 7 days. Monitoring hook & rollback policy in place.
- Stage 2: convert additional 10 reserved H100 -> A100 over 14 days if pilot meets success metrics.
- Hot-standby: keep 20 H100 on hot-standby (billed at 50% of committed H100 rate while unused, full rate if used).
- Expected commercial impact: ~20% reduction in baseline unit cost for committed tokens; billing proration applied to the month of change.
- Doc/Link: proposed_sku_shift_summary.pdf and a draft amendment (DocuSign link in HubSpot).

Operational notes:
- We'll need one telemetry milestone: a 48-hour post-pilot review capturing p50/p95, batch size distribution, and any fallback events.
- If Brightpath wants, we can also enable prefix caching for certain frequent request paths to further reduce token consumption — will include configuration in the kickoff.

Karthik Iyer
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Hi Olga / Karthik — thanks for the clear plan and the numbers.

We are comfortable with the pilot (convert 10 H100 -> A100-eq for 7 days) and the staged shift if telemetry looks good. A couple of items from procurement:
- Please confirm the exact proration calculation (line-item) for the month we convert capacity; procurement wants the month-level delta before signing.
- We request a 30-day pilot guarantee: if p95 increases >10% versus baseline during the pilot, Redwood will revert changes and credit the pro-rated difference for that pilot period.

If you can send the DocuSign amendment with those two clarifications, we will sign and schedule the kickoff for Nov 6. Also open to the prefix-caching recommendation — please include a short implementation checklist in the kickoff notes.

— Priya (on behalf of Brightpath Procurement)
